extraction.name: IFEval (Instruction-Following Eval)
extraction.description: IFEval is a benchmark for evaluating the instruction-following ability of large language models. It consists of around 541 prompts, each containing one or more verifiable instructions drawn from a set of 25 instruction types (e.g., 'write in more than 400 words', 'mention the keyword AI at least 3 times'). The benchmark enables automatic, objective, and reproducible evaluation without relying on human annotators or LLM-based evaluators.
extraction.creator: Jeffrey Zhou; Tianjian Lu; Swaroop Mishra; Siddhartha Brahma; Sujoy Basu; Yi Luan; Denny Zhou; Le Hou
extraction.citeAs: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou. Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models. arXiv:2311.07911, November 15, 2023.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Prompts were generated through a combination of few-shot prompting with a language model and manual human curation. Base prompts were created with randomly selected verifiable instructions appended, then filtered for illogical combinations via few-shot prompting, rephrased for diversity via another few-shot prompting step, and finally manually checked and edited one by one.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: GPT-4 and PaLM 2 Small (S) model responses collected via API calls; 541 prompts with verifiable instructions constructed through few-shot prompting and manual curation
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: GPT-4 responses collected in November 2023; PaLM 2 S responses collected in August 2023
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Human evaluation is noted to introduce potential biases and inconsistencies for reproducibility; LLM-based auto-evaluation is potentially biased or limited by the ability of the evaluator LLM
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Very few instructions are 100% verifiable objectively and automatically — there always exist edge cases where it is hard to determine if an instruction is followed; the loose criterion reduces false negatives but is likely to introduce false positives; the current implementation can be improved by increasing the diversity and quantity of verifiable instructions and extending to multi-modal use cases
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Discrepancies or misunderstandings in following instructions can lead to unintended outputs, which might have dire results, especially in crucial scenarios like healthcare or autonomous systems
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the instruction-following ability of large language models; enabling researchers to draw insights on what types of instructions are not usually followed; comparing different large language models on various instruction types
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Prompts were generated through a four-step process: (1) base prompts were created with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended; (2) few-shot prompting was used to identify and remove illogical or conflicting prompts; (3) another few-shot prompting approach was applied to rephrase each prompt to increase diversity of phrasing; (4) all rephrased prompts were manually checked and edited one by one. This process resulted in 541 prompts with varied phrasing and parameter variants for each verifiable instruction type.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Prompts were filtered to remove illogical ones using a few-shot prompting approach, then rephrased using another few-shot prompting step to increase phrasing diversity, and finally manually checked and edited one by one.
